scores.evidence: Phase 1: "Cost & Latency Gates + Guardrails"; Phase 2 "Retrieval Quality"; Phase 3 "Human-in-the-Loop Escalation + Pilot"
scores.rationale: Mostly substrate-upward with gates proven before next phase, but HITL comes after retrieval and the Phase 0 jailbreak and V-ID numbering are inconsistent (V2 cited as retrieval F1 and latency).

scores.evidence: "One real user question, end-to-end retrieval and LLM response, deployed to an internal staging environment, logged, monitored, and rolled back."
scores.rationale: Phase 0 is a genuine thin end-to-end slice with deploy, trace, and rollback, though staging/internal rather than full production.

scores.evidence: "LLM provider: API vs self-hosted | R2 ... | Default: API | ... | Flip condition: V1 fails → switch to self-hosted"
scores.rationale: Irreversible decisions are tabulated with reversibility, default, assumption, and flip conditions, plus labeled unknowns.

scores.evidence: "Phase 1 ... Cost gate V1 ... Latency gate V2 ... Guardrail validation V3 ... Rate limit & cost cap"
scores.rationale: Broad concerns (guardrails, budgets) precede leaf work across phases, but ordering within phases is not explicitly reasoned by blast radius and guardrail implementation is listed after measurement tasks.

scores.evidence: "Hard token cap (500 tokens). Jailbreak injection test" (Phase 0); Phase 1 injection filter; Phase 2 PII audit; Phase 3 ticket redaction; Phase 4 audit logging
scores.rationale: Security has concrete content in every phase starting from Phase 0.

scores.evidence: "Stdout/file logging: question, retrieved docs, response, cost, latency, tokens."
scores.rationale: Observability is present in Phase 0 and extended concretely in every later phase.

scores.evidence: "Docker image with pinned deps. Seed for FAISS index reproducible."
scores.rationale: Reproducibility is concretely addressed in all five phases (versioned index, gold dataset, scripted rollout).

scores.evidence: "Manual rollback tested (stop, revert, delete logs)." Phase 1: "Graceful degradation: if LLM API down, return cached answers or escalate."
scores.rationale: Phase 0 only has rollback, and real failure handling (retries, circuit breaker) arrives from Phase 1; reasonably threaded but Phase 0 lacks failure handling proper.
Defenses and budgets come early, but HITL is built after retrieval, and memory/orchestration/routing phasing is inconsistent with the required order.

scores.evidence: "Multi-model routing ... Pull forward: Cost baseline (V1) shows >$0.02 mean; A/B test ... cost reduction >20% with <5% accuracy loss."
scores.rationale: Six deferred items each have concrete pull-forward conditions.

note: Strong gates, skeleton, and threaded cross-cutting tables; weaknesses are the HITL-after-retrieval ordering, inconsistent gate IDs, and a preamble admitting missing reference files.
